Inflation expectations skyrocketing among Americans:

US consumers now expect inflation to rise to ~4.6% over the next year, the 3rd-highest reading over the last 12 months.

This is now 1.1 percentage points above the level seen at the start of 2026.

This comes as the proportion of consumers spontaneously mentioning gasoline as a concern rose to ~30%, its 4th-highest in at least 2 years.

At the same time, ~37% of consumers mentioned tariffs, the highest proportion since April.

Americans think another wave of inflation has begun.

Silver miners are sitting on a record cash pile:

Net cash balance across the top 10 silver mining companies surged to a record ~$4.2 billion in Q2 2026.

This figure has more than doubled since Q3 2025.

This marks a sharp reversal from the 2014-2024 period, when debt exceeded cash levels for most quarters.

To put this into perspective, during the 2010-2011 rally, combined net cash balance among these companies never exceeded $2.0 billion.

Cash accumulation has accelerated sharply alongside the silver rally, as higher silver prices have boosted margins and free cash flow across the group.

Silver miners have never been this liquid.

This also marks the largest quarterly increase on record.

Since the 2020 pandemic, this figure has surged +$83.9 trillion.

As a percentage of GDP, household net worth rose +20 percentage points last quarter, to 571%, just below the all-time high of 574% set in Q3 2021.

But when you talk to these people, you realize really quickly that there’s a difference in the way that different countries think about Bitcoin

They’ve even gotten completely more optimistic or pessimistic around different events throughout Bitcoin’s history. And this dynamic is exactly what we’re going to examine today.

The biggest issue with an AI "safety slowdown:"

What happens with China?

While there are legitimate concerns around the safety of AI and how quickly it is evolving, the AI race is global.

And, in today's ecosystem, falling even 6 months behind in the AI race is like falling decades behind in the pre-AI world.

If US AI giants agree to slow progress and focus on safety, there must be an international agreement in place as well.

And, even if there is an agreement in place, how do we regulate compliance?

We've said it before and we will say it again: AI is the biggest technological revolution in history.

This is an AI arms race that may be impossible to fully regulate.

China is attempting to refill its oil reserves.

Chinese crude imports rose +2.2 million tons in August, to 37.9 million tons, marking their 2nd consecutive monthly increase.

This brings the 2-month increase to ~9.0 million tons, or a ~33% recovery from the total drop between January and July this year.

The increase in crude supply has also allowed China to ramp up fuel exports, with overseas sales of gasoline and diesel surging +29% last month.

However, China's crude imports were down -23% year-over-year and -32% below this year's peak.

Meanwhile, China’s massive oil inventories are estimated at more than 1.2 billion barrels, giving the country ample flexibility to reduce purchases as prices rise.

China's massive oil stockpile is growing again.
